derived_request_schema_outputs_not_publi.reason: Per-request runtime-derived schemas are generated by published source; they are not copied, including unique output representatives. Normative schema source resources selected separately are retained.

limitations: Completeness is defined by the explicit source/resource inclusion and artifact exclusion rules, not by mirroring the whole experimental workspace.

Some excluded Python files are data materializers containing actual questions, source dialogue or manual model-output reviews. They remain local and are listed with hashes; their contents were not edited into artificial generic code.
Generated request schemas are reconstructible runtime outputs, and individual generated schema paths remain external until a run rebuilds them.
Historical scripts retain original absolute paths and immutable hashes. Inputs, frozen manifests, model/tokenizer/adapter artifacts, API settings and credentials are not supplied.
Cross-region Python references are reported as source strings; dynamic references driven by excluded run configuration/data cannot be proven closed by syntax inspection alone.

Additional semantic audit excluded mixed historical scripts whose algorithms embed actual source facts, private Gold or manual per-question reviews. In particular build_historical184.py and review_property_rules.py remain in the original local runtime; exact historical admission requires those restricted scripts and frozen inputs. Generic source publication is not a fully executable historical workspace.
Third-party reference copies with no verified distribution license are excluded; respective source URLs and file hashes are retained in the exclusion records.

post_selection_semantic_audit.reason: Read-only content audit found actual question/Gold/source-fact/review payloads embedded in Python or text. Mixed files are excluded whole rather than edited into a different method. Two BLIND_RAW_CAPTURED outputs had inclusion metadata but were never staged.

third_party_reference_audit.note: A local comparative README remains because it is project-authored; original third-party sources and example data are not included.
